about: Shared test vectors for the Study Desk's merge rules (src/lib/desk-merge.mjs; STUDY-DESK.md, 'When notes collide: rules a to e'). For each case, merging `incoming` into `local` as of `now` must give exactly `expect`, the whole notebook sorted by id, compared as JSON (key order does not matter). `local` is the side that is never clamped; `incoming` is the arriving side, which is clamped and checked. The clamp's cap is `now`, or the case's `exported` (when the arriving copy was saved, as an export file says) if that is earlier; an arriving record with any time past the cap (its `modified`, a trash record's `deletedAt`, or the `modified` of the copy a trash record holds) is written at the cap, and only when `local` has nothing for it: no record with its id, no trash record deleting it, and, for a trash record, neither the record it deletes nor another trash record deleting that. Version 2 (2026-10-26, audit FA1-c) added that never-beats rule, `exported`, the held copy's clamp, and skipping a record whose kind differs from another copy of its id, here or in the same input, or a trash record that names itself; two version 1 clamp cases lost their `local` records, which became cases of their own. Exact ties go to the local copy (no tiebreak is given). A case with `skipped` also says how many incoming records must be reported and not written. `rule` names the rule the case is about: a (newer writing wins), b (deleted on one side, edited on the other), c (30-day trash, then a tombstone), collapse (two trash records for one deletion; the website's proposal of 2026-10-12, not yet confirmed by the apps), keep (principle 6), clamp, skip, migrate. Version 3 (2026-11-02, STUDY-DESK.md E9, accepted by BDR 2026-10-23) added `migrate`: a bookmark gains an optional `follow: true`, its name is `label`, and a ribbon (a `place` with `ribbon: true` and a `name`, which only the website's preview ever wrote) is read as a bookmark on arrival, with the same id, `name` becoming `label` and `follow: true` added, and so is a ribbon held by a trash record, whose `deletedKind` becomes `bookmark`. Only arriving records are migrated, so a `migrate` case is one-sided (merging the other way round leaves the old shape in place). A client that never met a ribbon (the apps, which build bookmarks only) may skip the `migrate` cases, but should carry a `place` it doesn't understand untouched (the `keep` case). Version 4 (2026-11-04, audit 2 DI-3, DI-8, DI-12) added three cases and changed two rules, for BDR to confirm: two copies of one trash id merge field-wise (the later `deletedAt`, the later `modified`, and the held record with the later `modified`), not by picking a whole copy; an arriving time within five minutes of `now` is not "ahead" (a file's own `exported` time stays exact); and the cap is written as UTC with a `Z` however the file spelled it. A client that picks one whole trash copy will fail `collapse-one-trash-id-two-held-copies-keeps-the-newer-words`. Five cases added 2026-11-07 (audit 3 DI3-1 and DI3-5) under rules already here, so the version stands: a deletion stamped past the record it deletes and a restore stamped past the deletion it undoes, which every client's stamps must now guarantee (an edit past the version it replaces, a deletion past the record, a restore past the deletion, an undo past what it undoes, each by at least 1 ms; otherwise, within the five minutes of skew allowed, a deletion or a restore made on the slower clock is reversed when the copies meet), and an old iOS `star` marker read as `emphasis`, as `bookmark` is read as `ribbon`. Version 5 (2026-11-07, audit 3 DI3-3; BVJ's decision 2, for BDR to review) added the format's only field-level rule, confined to bookmarks: a bookmark carries `placedAt` (stamping `bookKey`, `chapter`, `verse`, `endVerse` and `contentVersion`) and `editedAt` (everything else), and two copies that both carry the stamps merge by group, the place from the later `placedAt`, the rest from the later `editedAt`, and `modified` and `client` from the later `modified`, a tie in any stamp settled as rule a settles one; a copy without both stamps merges whole by rule a, so an app that hasn't adopted them still syncs. A bookmark that moves as the reader reads is written every two seconds, so by the whole record a rename, a label or "Move as I read" turned off on another device always lost to the next move. `placedAt` and `editedAt` are clamped as `modified` is. The five `a-bookmark-` and `clamp-a-bookmark-` cases are its. Version 6 (2026-11-10, Audit 8 DI8-3; BVJ's decision 3, for BDR to review) carries the group merge into the trash: where two trash records for one deletion both hold stamped copies of a bookmark, or a live stamped bookmark meets a deletion that holds one, the held copy is merged by group as live copies are, so a rename on one device and a move on another both survive the deletion and a restore brings back the same bookmark everywhere. A tie in a group's stamp goes to the copy whose fields in that group sort first as canonical JSON (for the place, `placedAt` and the place fields; for the edit, every other field but `modified` and `client`; for the whole, `modified` and `client`), which keeps the result the same in any order. `collapse-two-held-copies-of-a-bookmark-merge-by-group` and `b-a-deletion-keeps-the-live-bookmark-s-newer-group` are its. Version 7 (2026-11-10, Audit 8 PC8B-2, which is DI6-5; BVJ's direction to go with the website's recommendation, for BDR to review) changes rule b for a bookmark carrying both stamps: it counts as edited at its `editedAt`, not its `modified`, so a move as the reader reads no longer undoes a deletion made elsewhere; a rename, a label, the "Move as I read" switch, a restore or an undo after the deletion still brings it back (a restore and an undo stamp `editedAt`). When the deletion stands, the trash holds the moved place, as version 6 merges a held bookmark by group. A bookmark without both stamps keeps the old rule. `b-a-followed-bookmark-s-move-leaves-its-deletion-standing` (with its `-other-way` twin) and `b-a-bookmark-renamed-after-its-deletion-comes-back` are its.

modules.verseCopy: Therefore, nothing is now a verdict against those connected with Christ Jesus, for the Torah of the Breath of Life liberated you with Christ Jesus from the torah of deviation and death. Since the Torah was unable to accomplish it while it was powerless under self-preservation, God sent God’s own son in the likeness of a human life shaped by self-preservation under deviation and rendered a verdict against deviation in self-preservation so that the Torah’s act of restorative justice would be fully lived out among us, those who do not walk based on self-preservation but based on Life-breath instead.
